_description: Statistical/numeric TABLE-RAG corpus: 2 dense US Census P60 reports — Poverty in the US 2022 (P60-280) + Health Insurance Coverage in the US 2022 (P60-281). Stresses the table-RAG / text-to-SQL + numeric-grounding path: specific table-cell retrieval, prose-numeric grounding, AGGREGATE/compute (the row-vs-aggregate fabrication boundary), + near-miss counterfactuals (a value that looks like it belongs but isn't in the table). Public-domain census.gov PDFs; sources LOCAL in ~/corpus-drop/census-stats, not committed.
_PARSE_NOTE: INGESTED WITH --force-docling (Docling/TableFormer), NOT the default PyMuPDF route. KEY FINDING: PyMuPDF's born-digital route MANGLES these dense Census tables (collapses rows/columns into run-on mega-cells → text-to-SQL gets garbage); Docling/TableFormer PRESERVES the structure (well-formed GFM, value-per-cell). => a parse-ROUTING fix candidate: route table-dense born-digital docs to Docling. ~12.6 min/doc.
_MISLABEL_NOTE: Filenames/slugs say 'income-p60-280' + 'poverty-p60-281' but the ACTUAL content (verified by H1) is Poverty (P60-280) + Health Insurance (P60-281) — I assumed the P60 numbering without verifying (a measure-don't-assert miss). doc_ids retain the wrong slug (load-bearing id); FRONTMATTER TITLES retitled to the correct content. Queries are content-valid (agents read the real content; verifier validated every value).
_authoring: generate(2 deep-readers)->adversarial-verify(per-candidate, 31-agent workflow `.claude/workflows/census-table-corpus-author.js`) — 29/29 survived, values verified verbatim against the Docling tables.
